analysis.title: Another distressing report, borderline disturbing
key_insights: Yesterday's US CPI printed hotter than expected: headline +0.4% m-o-m vs 0.3% consensus, core +0.3% vs 0.2% market view. Drivers cited: faster grocery and food inflation, persistent shelter pressure, and delayed pass-through of earlier energy shocks into medical care and household furnishings.
US rates reacted sharply: 2-year yields rose 19bps and 10-year yields rose 14bps, briefly back above 5%. A Bloomberg story raises the possibility of a 50bps Fed hike.

The yield spike followed a rush into Treasuries after the AI trade and the bullish oil trade hit an air pocket following last week's US election. The market read was that AI would slow and that peace in the Middle East is closer than war after the Democratic win.
Fed voter Goolsbee, usually dovish, called the CPI report 'another distressing report, borderline disturbing' and said the Fed had been hoping for progress.
AI: the Financial Times reports Anthropic's bankers are preparing to raise its IPO valuation to $1.5 trillion. Headlines are also swirling around the Nvidia CEO.

Iran: Trump says the US will continue a full sea and land economic blockade and that new strikes are 'highly unlikely'. The Jerusalem Post cites sources saying Qatar's prime minister told G7 foreign ministers Doha secured 'at least two weeks' to pursue an understanding between Washington and Tehran before US escalation.

Rabobank sees possible renewed fighting by mid- to end-November, when a third US aircraft carrier will be in the region. Logistics point to a high risk of conflict: the US moved 10 refuelling planes from a second UK airbase. Western intelligence says Iran can produce up to 50 missiles a month despite the blockade.

Yemen/Saudi: Syria denied reports that thousands of its troops were deployed to help Saudi forces against the Houthis. Syria is considering joining the Mecca Pact, in which Egyptian and Pakistani troops, French and British jets are already present in Saudi Arabia.

Russia, Ukraine and the US held talks in Abu Dhabi on a 'final end' to the war and a 'new European security architecture', without Europe present. Rabobank's best case is a frozen conflict. Worst cases are talks collapsing into escalation or, less likely, a US deal conceding a NATO roll-back to Russia.

Per Bloomberg, Russia has effectively abandoned efforts to replace the dollar with CNY because of US secondary sanctions. The yuan share of payments for Russian exports halved to 22%, and Russia now receives RUB for 69% of its exports to Asia.

Canadian PM Carney said China's security risks to Canada are 'much, much, much less' than those of the United States. Rabobank questions whether the new Democratic Congress will cut tariffs on Canada while Ottawa integrates more with China.

Dutch ECB president candidate Klaas Knot told the FT the ECB 'will not hesitate to take action' and would not rule out another 'more tailored instrument' in a future crisis. Today's calendar is quiet apart from ECB President Lagarde speaking.

tension_points.theme: Treasury yields after AI and peace trades
tension_points.bull_case: Markets rushed into Treasuries after last week's election on the view that the AI trade will slow and the Middle East is closer to peace than war.
tension_points.bear_case: Hot CPI sent 2-year yields up 19bps and 10-year yields up 14bps. Rabobank says that if the AI and peace assumptions are wrong, the outcome is worse, and cites a possible return to fighting by mid- to end-November.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A resumption of US-Iran fighting by mid- to end-November, or an AI trade that does not slow.

tension_points.bull_case: Best case is a frozen conflict, and Zelenskyy called the initial talks 'constructive and fairly substantive'.
tension_points.bear_case: Talks collapse and escalation resumes, or the US agrees to Russian demands for a NATO roll-back.

theme_stances.theme: US inflation and Fed hike risk
theme_stances.key_argument: The hotter CPI print, with progress on inflation absent, moved yields sharply and put a 50bps hike on the table.
Troop and logistics movements point to a high risk of renewed conflict by mid- to end-November despite stated diplomacy.
theme_stances.evidence: Other logistical movements point to a high risk of looming conflict.
